copy.blurb:
Switzerland face Canada on Wednesday, evening UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards on the Canada side, +13.0pp.

Elo numbers going in: Switzerland 1830, Canada 1860. That's a 30-point lead for Canada — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Switzerland to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Canada to win at 39%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Canada sits at 39% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Switzerland to win at 48%, the draw at 27%, and Canada to win at 26%. The Canada side trades at 26% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +285. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 39%, +13.0pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Canada side that lower bound is 32% — +5.8pp clear of the market's 26%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 33 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: This is a selection call on the Canada side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Canada side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
copy.summary: The model thinks Canada are mispriced. Our number reads 39% on the away side; the market reads 26%. The +13.0pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Switzerland v Canada · the model leans Canada
